protocol.name: cutefish_computer_control_v1

description.summary: let an agent drive the seat once the user allows it

protocol.description:
This protocol lets the Cutefish computer-use service move the pointer and type on the primary seat on behalf of an agent application, after the user has allowed it in a dialog the compositor asks for.
The compositor only advertises this global to the executables it trusts for this. Every other client never sees it.
Input sent through a control is handled like input from a device: window management, keyboard shortcuts, drags and pointer constraints all apply. Real input always wins: it releases whatever the control holds and pauses the control for a short while.

description.summary: asks for control of the seat

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager does not end the controls it created.

request.name: request_control
request.description:
Creates a control and asks the user whether the named agent may take over the pointer and keyboard. Exactly one of granted or revoked follows, in the user's own time.
Only one control exists at a time: while another is pending or granted, the new one is revoked with the busy reason at once.

arg.name: agent_name
arg.summary: the agent application's name, shown to the user

interface.name: cutefish_computer_control_v1
interface.description:
A control starts pending, becomes granted when the user allows it, and ends with revoked. A revoked control rejects every input request; asking again takes a new control, and a new answer from the user.
Rejections are sent while the request is handled, in request order, so a wl_display.sync after a batch of requests tells whether any of it was dropped.

entry.name: invalid_state
entry.summary: a button or key state is neither released nor pressed

entry.name: invalid_clipboard
entry.summary: the clipboard fd is not a regular file, or is too large

entry.name: denied
entry.summary: the user did not allow it

entry.name: busy
entry.summary: another control is pending or granted

entry.name: unavailable
entry.summary: the user could not be asked

entry.name: not_granted
entry.summary: the control is pending or revoked

entry.name: paused
entry.summary: the user is using the pointer or keyboard

entry.name: protected
entry.summary: the input would reach a dialog that answers for the user

entry.name: untypable
entry.summary: the text has characters the layout cannot type, and no text field takes them or it mixes them with control keys

entry.name: no_window
entry.summary: the window is gone or cannot take the window request

entry.name: other_desk
entry.summary: the window is on a desk that is not shown

request.name: destroy
request.description: Releases every button and key the control holds.

request.name: motion
request.description: Moves the pointer to a point in the compositor's global logical coordinate space, the one wl_output and xdg_output positions are in. Points outside every output are clamped to the nearest one.

request.name: button

description.summary: press or release a pointer button

request.description: The button is a Linux evdev code, e.g. BTN_LEFT. A press is rejected when the pointer is over a protected dialog. A release of a button this control pressed is never rejected; any other release is ignored.

request.name: axis
request.description: Scrolls by whole wheel clicks at the pointer; positive values scroll down and to the right.

request.name: key
request.description: The key is a Linux evdev code for the key as labelled on a PC keyboard, with no positional modifier swap: KEY_LEFTMETA is the Meta or Command key. A press is rejected while the keyboard focus is on a protected dialog. A release of a key this control pressed is never rejected; any other release is ignored.

request.name: keysym

description.summary: press or release the key that types a keysym

request.description: Presses or releases the key that types the keysym on the current keyboard layout, without the Shift or AltGr level it may need: the client names a shortcut's modifiers itself. It is how a shortcut written with a character, such as Ctrl+Z, reaches the key labelled with it on any layout. A press is rejected as untypable when the layout has no such key, and as the key request's press otherwise; the release releases the key the press pressed.

request.name: type_text
request.description: Types UTF-8 text into whatever has the keyboard focus. Line feeds, tabs and backspaces are typed as Return, Tab and Backspace. When the current keyboard layout has every other character, the string is typed as key strokes, with Shift or AltGr as needed; otherwise all of it is committed to the focused text field at once, since clients may apply a commit before keys sent earlier. The whole string is rejected as untypable, and nothing typed, when it needs a commit and no text field has the focus, or when it needs a commit and has line feeds, tabs or backspaces: send those parts separately, giving the client time to handle each.

request.name: list_windows
request.description: Sends a window event for every application window, most recently used first, then windows_done. Rejected as not_granted, with no window events, unless the control is granted.

request.name: activate_window
request.description: Brings the window forward and gives it the focus, as the user's click on its application in the dock does: a minimized or hidden window comes back and a window on another desk brings its desk up. The handle is one a window event of this control named. Rejected as no_window when that window is gone, and as an input request would be otherwise.

request.name: get_pointer
request.description: Sends a pointer event, or is rejected as not_granted unless the control is granted.

request.name: close_window
request.description: Asks the window to close, as its close button does; the application may ask the user first. A window that stopped responding is killed. Rejected as no_window when the window is gone or cannot be closed, as protected when it belongs to the process that shows system dialogs, and as an input request would be otherwise.

request.name: set_window_frame
request.description: Moves the window's frame to the given geometry in the global logical coordinate space. A maximized, full-screen or snapped window becomes a normal one. The size is kept within the window's limits, and kept as it is when the window cannot be resized; the frame is kept on screen enough to grab. Rejected as no_window when the window is gone, minimized, hidden or on another desk, and as close_window is otherwise.

request.name: set_clipboard
request.description: Replaces the clipboard with the text, as copying it would; the agent pastes it with the application's shortcut. The fd is a regular file, such as a memfd, holding UTF-8 text of at most 16 MiB; the compositor reads it at once and closes it. The text is offered as text/plain;charset=utf-8, text/plain, UTF8_STRING, STRING and TEXT. Rejected as an input request would be.

event.name: granted
event.description: Input requests take effect from now on.

event.name: revoked
event.description: Buttons and keys the control held have been released. The control is inert from now on; the client should destroy it.

event.name: window
event.description: The handle stays the same for the window as long as the control exists. The geometry is the window's frame in the global logical coordinate space, and means nothing while the window is minimized, hidden or on another desk.

event.name: pointer
event.description: In the global logical coordinate space.
